ri_buddy_boulder.blurb: A single large boulder in Lincoln Woods State Park, several miles north of Providence, sitting close to the road behind Ship's Prow. Ten bouldering problems span a friendly range: four at V0, a pair around V1, then a V3 and a V4 on the main face, a V6, and a V10-level line at the very top end. The easy slab and arete lines make it a good spot to warm up, and a traverse on the back side adds variety. It is quick to reach, so it fits easily into a longer Lincoln Woods session.

_expect.name: Trailside (The Scoop and the Pine Line area).

ri_trailside_the_scoop_and_the_pine_line.blurb: A small bouldering spot along the Mt. Tom trail in Rhode Island's Arcadia Management Area, on granite ledges tucked below the path. Ten problems run from VB up to V3, mostly vertical faces with decent holds, which makes it a relaxed place to warm up or to climb with newer boulderers. One tall highball here has its crux near the top and only comes into condition after a dry spell because water drains down it. Some lines are lichenous and could use a brushing before you try them.

ri_escoheag_boulder_the.blurb: One freestanding boulder, around 15 feet tall, in the Escoheag section of Arcadia Management Area in southwest Rhode Island. It holds ten bouldering problems with a broad spread: one each from V1 through V5, a couple at V6, two at V8, and a V9 at the top. Both stand starts and sit starts are part of the mix, so easier and harder versions share the same features. The boulder is a short walk in from the end of the dead-end spur along a wide trail, making it an easy stop for a focused session.

sd_lies_boulder.blurb: The first boulder you meet in the Roadside Jumble, part of the Needles of Rushmore climbing near Mount Rushmore National Memorial in South Dakota. It sits only a few steps from where you leave the car. Ten bouldering problems cover a solid spread: four around V2, a pair at V3, then a V4, a V5, a V6 and a V8 at the top. A handful of strong lines make it worth the stop, including a long sloper traverse that stands out from the rest, so it suits a quick session or a warm-up for nearby climbing.

tn_slide_the.blurb: One of the boulders at Boulders on Old Wauhatchie Pike, a public bouldering park beside Chattanooga's St. Elmo neighborhood at the foot of Lookout Mountain. It earned its name from a waterslide that once stood on the property. Ten problems run from V0 to a hard V8 end, with most in the V1 to V4 range, up a blunt prow, a groove, an arete and a face leading to a hueco on the upper section. Pads are useful on both sides of the arete, and the mix of grades suits a mixed group.

tx_mopboys.blurb: A bouldering area on North Mountain at Hueco Tanks in far west Texas, built around two features about 100 feet apart: a long chalked traverse wall and a steep roof. Ten problems range from VB to V12, but the bulk are around V2 to V4, with a single V9 and a V12 for hard climbers. The traverse wall gets early sun and then sits in shade most of the day, while the roof is shaded early and sunny for most of the day, so you can pick a side to suit the temperature.
